## The best of Central America in 24 days: an itinerary through six countries

Our journey begins in Guatemala and ends in Panama, passing through **Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua and Costa Rica** in between. Over 24 days and 23 nights, travelers explore Maya cultural heritage, volcanic landscapes, rainforests and cloud forests, colonial cities and the natural environment of Central America's ocean-facing regions.

This itinerary involves extensive travel, several international borders, domestic flights and changing natural conditions. It is well suited to people ready to devote full days to excursions and keen to discover different parts of the region on a single journey. For a shorter trip focused on archaeological monuments, consider the [12-day Guatemala–Honduras–Belize program](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-honduras-belize/). Those preferring Costa Rican forests and several beach days can compare the [13-day Costa Rica and Nicaragua journey](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua/).

## The order in which the countries are visited

| Days | Country and highlights |
|---|---|
| 1–7 | Guatemala: Antigua, Atitlán, Tikal |
| 8 | Honduras: Copán |
| 9–11 | El Salvador: monuments and cities |
| 11–13 | Nicaragua: León, Masaya, Granada |
| 13–18 | Costa Rica: volcanoes, forests, ocean |
| 18–24 | Panama: Boquete, the capital, coast |

Days involving border crossings appear under both countries in the table: departure from one and entry into the next happen on the same calendar day. These rows must not simply be added as six independent tours with six separate sets of overnight stays. The logistics join them into one continuous itinerary.

The price includes **two domestic flights: Guatemala City–Flores and David–Panama City**. Most other travel is overland or by water. The itinerary also includes a crossing during the transfer from El Salvador to Nicaragua. Connections and border formalities matter on a journey like this: precise ground and water transport schedules must be agreed for the chosen dates.

## Guatemala: Antigua, Atitlán and Tikal

The journey begins in [Antigua Guatemala](/guatemala/place/antigua-guatemala/), whose historic center dates from the Spanish colonial period. This is followed by a visit to [Pacaya Volcano](/guatemala/place/pacaya-volcano/) and [Lake Atitlán](/guatemala/place/lake-atitlan/), with boat excursions to the communities of San Juan La Laguna and Santiago Atitlán.

Another stop is [Chichicastenango](/guatemala/place/chichicastenango/), famous for its trading and craft traditions. **A market visit is scheduled only on Thursday or Sunday.** This is particularly important when selecting the departure date: the daily sequence must be aligned with the calendar if the market is to remain part of the itinerary.

Travelers then fly from Guatemala City to Flores to explore the archaeological complex at [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/). Tall temples and ancient plazas stand amid tropical forest. The itinerary then visits [Río Dulce](/guatemala/place/rio-dulce/) and Livingston, followed by Quiriguá with its famous carved stelae.

## Honduras and El Salvador: the history of ancient cities

The main Honduran stop is [Copán](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/), one of the most important archaeological centers of Maya civilization. Its stone sculpture and Hieroglyphic Stairway are especially noteworthy. A visit to Copán complements Tikal: the two sites display different architectural and artistic traditions, though both belong to the same broader cultural world.

The itinerary then continues into El Salvador. Via San Salvador, travelers visit the archaeological sites of San Andrés and [Joya de Cerén](/el-salvador/place/joya-de-ceren/). UNESCO describes Joya de Cerén as a farming settlement preserved under volcanic ash. Unlike monumental Maya temples, it is valued for evidence of ordinary daily life: buildings, objects and traces of residents' activities. It is a rare opportunity to understand Central American history beyond its rulers and ceremonial centers.

The route then heads via the La Unión area into Nicaragua. Since this crossing involves changing countries and modes of transport, the day needs time for border controls, port procedures and onward travel.

## Nicaragua: León, Masaya Volcano and Granada

In Nicaragua, the route passes through [León](/nicaragua/place/leon/), Managua and [Granada](/nicaragua/place/granada/). The two historic cities offer an introduction to Spanish colonial heritage, while [Masaya Volcano](/nicaragua/place/masaya-volcano-national-park/) provides a nature-focused element.

Access to volcanic areas can change because of natural activity and safety requirements. When choosing dates, consider whether viewpoints are open; a volcano being named on the itinerary does not in itself guarantee a climb or access to a particular place near the crater.

After Granada, the journey crosses into Costa Rica. The Nicaraguan stage is relatively short, so when selecting a program, it is worth deciding whether cultural stops are the main interest or whether more time should be allocated to a single country's natural areas and beaches.

## Costa Rica: Arenal, Caño Negro and Monteverde

The journey's nature program is especially rich in Costa Rica. Around [Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/), travelers can see volcanic landscapes and tropical forest. The route then continues to the [Caño Negro reserve](/costa-rica/place/cano-negro-wildlife-refuge/), where excursions on the water offer opportunities to observe birds and other animals. Wildlife watching is never certain: sightings of particular species cannot be promised for a fixed date.

Next come the cloud forests of [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/), where walks and active experiences are included. The route then heads toward the Tárcoles River and the coast at [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/). Over a relatively short distance, travelers encounter humid forests at different altitudes before reaching the Pacific Ocean. This matters when packing: mountain areas may be cooler, while the coast is usually hot and humid.

The journey then enters Panama and continues toward Boquete.

## Panama: Boquete, Barú Volcano, the capital and an ocean-side finish

The Panama stage starts in [Boquete](/panama/place/boquete/), a mountainous region with coffee plantations and nature trails. A visit to [Barú Volcano](/panama/place/baru-volcano/) follows, with a 4×4 jeep excursion mentioned in the program. Mountain travel depends on route conditions and weather; visibility from higher altitudes can vary.

From David, travelers fly to [Panama City](/panama/place/panama-city/). The next sightseeing day includes [Chagres National Park](/panama/place/chagres-national-park/) and a visit to an Emberá village before the group heads to Panama's Pacific Riviera. The final free days are reserved for relaxing before departure.

The journey therefore ends at a gentler pace than it begins: after the busy stages of borders, excursions and transfers, there are days without a packed schedule.

## Who will enjoy such a long itinerary

This is a journey for travelers who want **an extensive geographical and cultural introduction to Central America**, rather than a week at a single resort. In 24 days, you can see ancient Maya cities, colonial quarters, volcanic plateaus, nature reserves and coastlines, but such breadth comes at the cost of time spent in transit. Frequent hotel changes and early starts inevitably become part of the experience.

When choosing the time of year, weather in one capital is not enough. The Guatemalan highlands, Costa Rica's humid forests and Panama's Pacific coast differ in temperature and rainfall. Conditions at volcanoes and on boat excursions also matter. The market schedule at Chichicastenango needs to be considered separately from the climate.

## Included services and questions before booking

The price includes a Russian-speaking guide, transfers along the route, hotel accommodation, scheduled excursions, accommodation taxes and **the Guatemala City–Flores and David–Panama City flights**. Meals are included according to the arrangements for each specific day: breakfast, lunch and dinner must not be assumed included every day. Additional activities, airport charges and personal expenses are paid separately.

Arranging this journey starts with travel documents. Entry and transit requirements must be checked **for all six countries according to each traveler's nationality**, including re-entry conditions, passport validity, border fees and possible flight connections. Rules can change, so universal visa lists that do not specify nationality and the exact route should not be relied upon.

It is also sensible to check domestic flight schedules, the actual duration of overland and water crossings, access to individual volcanic areas and the day of the week for Chichicastenango market. This helps preserve the purpose of the main stops when planning specific dates.

## Frequently asked questions about the grand Central America tour

### How many countries are included in the mandatory itinerary?

Six: Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica and Panama. Belize is not listed as part of the mandatory itinerary of this 24-day journey.

### Are all 24 days filled with excursions?

No. Alongside the many excursion and transfer days, the program ends with several days of relaxation on Panama's coast.

### Which domestic flights are included?

Two flights: Guatemala City–Flores and David–Panama City. Other travel, including crossing national borders, is arranged overland or by water along the itinerary.

### Why does Chichicastenango market need to be visited on a particular day?

The current program schedules market visits on Thursday or Sunday. The departure date and order of visits therefore affect whether this stop can be included.

### Can the same entry rules be used throughout the route?

No. Each country has its own requirements based on nationality and the mode of entry. All six countries, as well as any transit points on flights, must be checked separately.

## “Best of Guatemala”: why the itinerary takes 14 days and includes Honduras

The tour's name highlights [Guatemala](/guatemala/), but its full geographical scope covers **two countries**: Guatemala and [Honduras](/honduras/). Over 14 days and 13 nights, travelers explore colonial Antigua, volcanic landscapes, communities around Lake Atitlán, Maya archaeology, the forested regions of central Guatemala, the Caribbean coast and ancient Copán across the border.

This journey is ideal for those who want to discover **different parts of the country on one itinerary**, rather than limit themselves to the most famous temples. Archaeology is important, but the schedule also includes natural landmarks, markets and coastal towns.

## Which stages need their own time

| Region | Main experience |
| --- | --- |
| Antigua and Atitlán | Cities, volcano and Maya communities |
| Chichicastenango | Highland market and traditions |
| Cobán | Reserve, Semuc Champey and caves |
| Petén and Tikal | Archaeology in tropical forest |
| Caribbean coast | Río Dulce and Livingston |
| Honduras | Ancient Copán and the return journey |

Most of these sections involve overland travel. Moving between highlands, forest and coast means changes in temperature, humidity and road conditions, so pack with several types of excursions in mind.

## The opening days: Antigua, Pacaya Volcano and Lake Atitlán

The itinerary starts with a transfer from Guatemala City to [Antigua Guatemala](/guatemala/place/antigua-guatemala/), a city of preserved colonial architecture against a backdrop of volcanoes. After exploring the city, the plan includes the [Pacaya Volcano](/guatemala/place/pacaya-volcano/) area and a transfer to [Lake Atitlán](/guatemala/place/lake-atitlan/).

At Atitlán, travelers meet the communities of San Juan La Laguna and [Santiago Atitlán](/guatemala/place/santiago-atitlan/). The distinctive feature of this stage is its interest in community life, crafts and traditions, rather than viewpoints alone. It combines a cultural day in town with travel into the countryside and outdoor activities.

Before visiting an active volcano, check access rules, weather and instructions from local guides. Changes in volcanic activity may affect the excursion route.

## Chichicastenango: why the day of the week matters

In [Chichicastenango](/guatemala/place/chichicastenango/), you visit the famous highland market. **Under the tour conditions, the market is visited on Thursday or Sunday.** Take this limitation into account when selecting the start date for the entire journey: the visit cannot simply be moved to any other day without modifying the program.

The market is known for textiles, handmade goods and the living traditions of local communities. To browse the stalls comfortably, plan what you need to carry that day and bring some small-denomination cash for purchases; payment methods depend on individual vendors.

## Central Guatemala: Cobán, Semuc Champey and caves

Midway through the journey, you move into wetter natural regions. Following the quetzal reserve, the plan includes [Cobán](/guatemala/) and a journey to [Semuc Champey](/guatemala/place/semuc-champey/), famous for its cascades of natural pools. The route then passes through the Candelaria cave system and continues toward Flores.

These days are very different from walking around Antigua. You will encounter uneven trails, humid air and long transfers between natural sites. Comfortable non-slip shoes and light rain protection are sensible; the difficulty of particular sections and actual physical exertion should be agreed based on road conditions and the chosen excursion.

## Tikal, Río Dulce and Copán: three distinct experiences

Day nine includes [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/), one of the largest Maya archaeological complexes. Its temples and plazas lie within protected tropical forest. UNESCO recognizes both its cultural and natural significance: the visit brings ancient architecture together with the ecosystem of Petén.

After the archaeological stage, the group heads toward [Río Dulce](/guatemala/place/rio-dulce/) and Livingston on the Caribbean coast. This is a different part of Guatemala, with a river, coastal communities and humid tropical landscapes.

Day twelve includes crossing into [Honduras](/honduras/) to visit [Copán](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/). This is a separate archaeological stop, not a site within Guatemala. Therefore, before booking, check entry and return requirements for your nationality and flight itinerary.

## Included services and who this tour suits

The tour includes **a Russian-speaking guide, scheduled transfers and excursions, accommodation in the specified hotels, accommodation taxes and meals on the designated days**. Optional activities, airport charges and personal purchases are listed as separate expenses. The air-ticket package should be checked against the final offer because the list of included services does not confirm every possible international flight.

This 14-day journey is particularly suited to people who want to add **Semuc Champey, caves, nature reserves and the Caribbean coast** to Maya history. If the priority is to explore archaeological centers and living Maya culture in a shorter time, compare the [10-day “Maya World” itinerary](/multi-country/tour/maya-world/). Both tours enter Honduras, but they reveal different aspects of the region.

## Frequently asked questions about the “Best of Guatemala” tour

### Is Honduras included?

Yes. A visit to Copán in Honduras is scheduled in the final days, after which the route returns to Guatemala City.

### When can Chichicastenango market be visited?

Under the itinerary conditions, the market can be visited on Thursday or Sunday. The dates should be agreed before arranging the journey.

### How is this tour different from “Maya World”?

It lasts 14 days and includes more natural areas alongside archaeology: the quetzal reserve, Semuc Champey, Candelaria Cave, Río Dulce and Livingston.

### Do I need special footwear?

Comfortable shoes with good grip are needed for nature trails and wet surfaces. Exact conditions for visiting the volcano, pools and cave depend on weather and local site operations.

## Bolivia and Chile in 16 days: from the Uyuni Salt Flat to Patagonia

This **16-day, 15-night** itinerary begins in [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) and ends in Santiago de Chile. In between are the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons, [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/), San Rafael Glacier, the [Marble Caves](/chile/place/marble-caves/), VIK winery and the Pacific coast.

The combination of northern high plateaus and southern Patagonia is particularly compelling. This journey is for people who want to experience both famous landmarks and dramatic changes in natural landscapes. It does require coping with altitude, road transfers and several domestic flights. More demanding physical activities should be assessed in advance.

Travel dates: **December 29–January 13**, with no confirmed departure year. This schedule includes New Year's Eve on the route between Bolivia and Chile. The year, price and full range of services are confirmed when the journey is agreed.

## The geography of the itinerary

| Part of the journey | Highlights |
| --- | --- |
| La Paz | A city at high altitude |
| Uyuni | Salt flat and lagoons |
| Atacama | Geysers and desert |
| Santiago | Chile's capital |
| Torres del Paine | Mountains and lakes |
| Aysén | Glacier and marble cliffs |
| Central Chile | Wine and coast |

The journey involves 2 major southbound transfers within Chile. First comes a flight from Calama to Santiago after Atacama, followed by a flight to the Puerto Natales area; later, travelers continue to Aysén for outings on the water. It should therefore not be mistaken for an uninterrupted road trip from Bolivia to Patagonia: distances are covered by combining flights, off-road vehicles and ground transfers.

## Bolivia's Altiplano: stunning scenery with the challenge of altitude

[La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) is already at a considerable elevation at the start of the journey. The route then climbs toward [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) and the Altiplano's geothermal areas. The Sol de Mañana geysers sit at **over 4,900 m**. This affects physical well-being more profoundly than the distance walked.

During the first days, avoid suddenly increasing exertion and pay attention to rest and hydration. Anyone with heart or lung conditions or other risk factors should discuss traveling to such altitudes with a doctor before paying. Symptoms of altitude sickness require medical assessment before continuing; a comfortable hotel or private vehicle does not eliminate the altitude.

The sky's mirror-like reflection on the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) is possible when a thin layer of water covers the surface. In the rainy season, some sections become impassable, so the spectacular mirror and a visit to Incahuasi Island cannot both be promised as a guaranteed scenario. Off-road routes are adjusted according to actual salt-flat and road conditions.

## Atacama: a different climate and pace after Bolivia's lagoons

Travel between the countries crosses a high-altitude border and continues to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). Activities include the [El Tatio geysers](/chile/place/el-tatio-geysers/) and Moon Valley. Early departures to the geysers generally require warm clothing, while the strong daytime sun and dry air feel very different. A jacket, hat, UV protection and drinking water are useful well before Patagonia.

An international road crossing cannot be measured solely in kilometers: time is required for document checks, border-post operating hours and weather or road delays. Ada Tours clarifies the precise entry requirements for Bolivia and Chile according to each traveler's nationality and itinerary dates; permission to enter one country does not guarantee the right to cross both borders.

## Southern Chile: two distinct parts of Patagonia

After Santiago, the journey moves to [Puerto Natales and Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/). An entire day is devoted to Mylodon Cave, lakes and panoramic stops around the national park. Granite towers and glacial lakes are the principal sights here. A sightseeing excursion requires protection from wind and rain; mountain weather can change visibility quickly.

The itinerary then heads farther into the Aysén region and toward [Puerto Río Tranquilo](/chile/place/puerto-rio-tranquilo/). Unlike better-known Torres del Paine, this section centers on water, rocks and remote roads. A boat excursion in the area of [Laguna San Rafael National Park](/chile/place/laguna-san-rafael-national-park/) starts from Exploradores Valley. It is important to distinguish the boat trip to San Rafael Glacier from a walk to Exploradores Glacier: access to the latter is restricted because of unstable ice, while our program specifies a boat outing toward San Rafael.

The following day is devoted to the [Marble Caves](/chile/place/marble-caves/) on General Carrera Lake. These arches and caverns were formed by water over a long period; their color changes with light and reflections. A **private boat** is scheduled for roughly 2.5 hours. Departure conditions depend on wind, waves and the local operator's decision, so even a private excursion cannot take place in all weather.

## Why flexibility matters on a New Year itinerary

Late December and early January fall in Patagonia's summer, but summer does not mean reliably calm weather. Strong winds and rain are possible in southern Chile, while precipitation on the Bolivian plateau can affect access to Uyuni. A single journey may require light clothing for Santiago, insulation for high-altitude areas and a waterproof jacket for the boat near San Rafael.

The itinerary lists flights from La Paz to Uyuni, Calama to Santiago, Santiago to Puerto Natales, Punta Arenas to Balmaceda, and Balmaceda to Santiago. Connections, baggage rules for the carriers involved, local transfers and alternatives in adverse weather should all be agreed before departure. Aysén's remoteness makes an overly tight schedule especially costly; boat days are best planned with a realistic buffer.

## The final days: VIK winery, Valparaíso and Santiago

Following the nature-focused stages, the itinerary returns to central Chile. A tour and lunch are planned at [VIK winery](/chile/place/vik-winery/) in Millahue Valley. This is followed by a visit to [Valparaíso and Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/), where vineyards, coastal hills and port architecture replace the high-altitude scenes of previous days.

The last free day is in Santiago. It is useful after such a busy itinerary, but should not automatically be treated as a guaranteed spare day for moving an excursion from distant Aysén: domestic flights and hotels may require changes to several subsequent stages.

## Accommodation and prices: what is already known

The trip covers 15 nights, but hotels and categories are specified in detail **for only the first 14**. Options listed include Casa Grande Suites in La Paz, Glamping Uyuni Deluxe on Uyuni, Nayara Alto Atacama, Mandarin Oriental Santiago, Singular Patagonia and Mallin Colorado Ecolodge or a similar property in Aysén. The hotel and category for the last night in Santiago are still to be confirmed. BB means breakfast.

**No single fixed total price is given for this itinerary.** The final price is calculated after agreement on dates, hotels and services. Although the program lists specific domestic flights, one must not assume that all tickets are automatically included in the base rate: inclusion, flight times, guides, admission tickets and other excursion costs are clarified in the complete commercial offer.

Before booking, request a unified calculation covering flights, transfers, accommodation, boat days, entrance fees, guiding languages and meals. Lunch is provided on some days, but no universal meal plan applies to the entire journey.

## Frequently asked questions about the Bolivia–Chile route

### Can I see Uyuni's mirror effect around New Year?

Reflections depend on the amount of water on the salt flat. During the rains, some roads and access to Incahuasi Island may be restricted. Conditions are checked before departure, so a particular photographic scene cannot be promised.

### Are there difficult mountain climbs on this journey?

The main program includes sightseeing, off-road travel, walks and boat outings. No technical ascent is listed. The principal medical factor is **the altitude of Bolivia's Altiplano**, especially the geyser area above 4,900 m, along with the duration of transfers.

### Is the Marble Caves boat outing private?

A private boat is specified for the Marble Caves excursion. The type of vessel and number of participants for the San Rafael Glacier trip are confirmed separately. These are different excursion days with different conditions.

### In what year will the trip take place, and what does it cost?

The dates are **December 29–January 13**, but the departure year and final price have not been established. Ada Tours agrees on these together with transport, accommodation and included services.

## Brazil and Argentina in 14 days: the Amazon, Iguazu and Buenos Aires

This Ada Tours program brings together urban landmarks and natural regions of South America. Over **14 days and 13 nights**, the journey visits 2 main countries: [Brazil](/brazil/) and [Argentina](/argentina/). You start in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), continue to the [Amazon](/brazil/place/manaus-amazon/), visit Salvador and the beaches of Praia do Forte, explore the Brazilian side of [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and finish in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/).

Flights alternate with river and forest activities, colonial architecture and sightseeing in major cities. The route suits travelers who want to discover several different regions of Brazil and finish with the atmosphere of Argentina's capital.

## The first 3 days: Rio from two heights

The Rio program begins with arrival and rest after the journey. A visit to Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado follows. From the viewpoint, the city spreads between mountains and ocean. Another day brings a visit to Sugarloaf Mountain: the cable car passes through Urca to the summit, with views over Guanabara Bay and the beach districts.

These are two different views of Rio. Corcovado lets visitors see the city from beside the monument, while Sugarloaf reveals its coastline, bays and neighborhoods. The sightseeing days also provide a sense of the distances and transport arrangements of this vast city.

## Manaus and the Amazon: what happens in the forest

The next stage begins with a flight to Manaus. The program leaves the large city behind for an Amazon lodge. In the forest, you will discover the vegetation and local way of life, visit a caboclo home and see how manioc flour is prepared.

The itinerary also includes Acajatuba village and an evening opportunity to watch animals along the riverbanks. The change in surroundings is an important part of the experience: days here are shaped not only by transport schedules but also by the river ecosystem, weather and the forest itself. Wildlife watching depends on conditions and does not guarantee an encounter with a particular species.

**The Meeting of the Waters of the Rio Negro and Solimões** is offered as a separate excursion **for $150 per person**. It is not included in the base price. The site is famous for differently colored currents flowing side by side for a while before mixing.

## Salvador, Praia do Forte and Iguazu

After the Amazon, the journey continues to [Salvador](/brazil/place/salvador/). A sightseeing excursion introduces the historic Pelourinho district, religious architecture and Bahia's cultural heritage. There is then a stop at [Praia do Forte](/brazil/place/praia-do-forte/) for time by the ocean.

Next comes Foz do Iguaçu. The tour includes a visit to **the Brazilian side of the waterfalls**, offering broad panoramic views of the cascades. This distinction matters when comparing tours: visiting both sides of Iguazu must be confirmed separately in the program because they are in different countries. On this route, the principal waterfall day is on the Brazilian side.

In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), the schedule includes a city tour of the principal districts and squares, followed by dinner and a tango show in the evening. The final day is set aside for the transfer to the airport.

## Daily itinerary overview

| Days | Main stage |
|---|---|
| 1–3 | Rio de Janeiro |
| 4–5 | Manaus and the Amazon |
| 6–8 | Salvador and Praia do Forte |
| 9–10 | Foz do Iguaçu |
| 11–14 | Buenos Aires |

The itinerary involves transfers between several distant regions of Brazil. Before booking, assess the flights and number of connections, not just the journey's total duration.

## Prices, included services and additional expenses

**Tour price: $3260.** The price includes accommodation, guided group excursions, transfers with a driver and admission tickets.

Flights listed along the itinerary are paid separately, at an estimated cost of **around $750 per person**, as are personal expenses and optional excursions. The excursion to the Meeting of the Waters of the Rio Negro and Solimões costs **$150 per person** and is an optional service.

| Included | Paid separately |
|---|---|
| Accommodation, excursions, transfers | Listed flights |
| Admission tickets | Optional excursions |
| Guided group excursions | Personal expenses |

If necessary, Ada Tours may replace a hotel with another of the same category. The order of excursions may also change while preserving the tour program. Conditions can be reviewed in the detailed itinerary for each day.

## Who this route suits

This journey is designed for travelers interested in both forest nature and large cities. It is different from a beach-only holiday: there are several flights, a forest lodge and various kinds of excursions. If the Amazon is your sole objective, an extensive itinerary that includes Salvador and Argentina may be more than you need.

For another combination of nature and culture, explore [multi-country trips](/multi-country/) and [tours in Brazil](/brazil/tour/). Choose according to the actual daily activities, duration and included services.

## Frequently asked questions about the Brazil and Argentina tour

### How long is the journey?

The program lasts 14 days and 13 nights, starting in Rio de Janeiro and ending in Buenos Aires.

### Are flights between cities included?

The listed domestic and international flights are treated as additional expenses. The description gives an estimated cost of around $750 per person.

### Are both sides of Iguazu visited?

The main waterfall day takes place on the Brazilian side. A visit to the Argentine walkways should not be regarded as included without separate confirmation.

## Rio Champions' Parade 2027 and three countries in 10 days

The program's main event is **the 2027 Carnival Champions' Parade at the Sambadrome in Rio de Janeiro**. According to organizer LIESA's published schedule, the winners' evening takes place on **February 13, 2027**. Unlike the main competition nights, this is when the highest-ranking samba schools perform. The journey combines Carnival night with Iguazu Falls, tango in Buenos Aires and a sightseeing tour of Santiago.

The route lasts **10 days and 9 nights**. Arrival dates are February 12–21; the precise schedule and Carnival arrangements are confirmed when booking. There are three main countries: Brazil, Argentina and Chile. An excursion to Uruguay is available only as an optional addition from Buenos Aires.

## What the included Sambadrome ticket provides

Travelers spend the first three nights in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). On Champions' Parade day, the itinerary features a four-hour excursion to Sugarloaf Mountain and the old city center, followed by time to rest before the evening show. At night, the Sambadrome fills with samba schools, elaborate costumes, floats and drumming groups.

**The tour price includes a ticket to the Champions' Parade and transfers hotel–Sambadrome–hotel.** The specific seating sector and transfer times are agreed at booking. A seat in any chosen stand or a private box must not automatically be considered an included service.

The following day is devoted to Corcovado and Christ the Redeemer. The tourist train travels through Tijuca Forest; the viewpoint looks out over Guanabara Bay, city districts and Sugarloaf Mountain. An additional evening at Marius restaurant is offered for an extra charge, as are other activities during free time.

## How the ten days are distributed

| Days | Destination and event |
|---|---|
| 1–3 | Rio and Champions' Parade |
| 4–5 | Brazilian Iguazu |
| 6–7 | Buenos Aires |
| 8–10 | Santiago and departure |

After Rio, a flight to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) is included. Day five includes an excursion on the Brazilian side of the waterfalls. Day six brings a border crossing to [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), a walk along the Argentine trails and a flight onward to Buenos Aires. This sequence allows you to see the cascades from afar and then get closer to individual falls.

Buenos Aires includes sightseeing with a Russian-speaking guide and a tango show with dinner and Argentine wines. After flying to Chile, the journey concludes with an introduction to [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and the flight home.

There are several short stops on this journey, combining a musical celebration with classic natural highlights of South America. The program does not include a long beach holiday or an independent expedition to Patagonia.

## Iguazu: the principal excursion and paid extras

The Brazilian and Argentine national parks lie on opposite sides of the same waterfall system. The Brazilian visit is built around panoramic viewpoints, while the Argentine side provides trails and platforms near the Devil's Throat. These are different experiences, so a visit to one side cannot replace the two excursions on the itinerary.

You can optionally add a Macuco Safari boat ride, [Bird Park](/brazil/place/parque-das-aves/) or a helicopter flight. These activities **are not included in the base price**. The original rate information gives different amounts for the same optional activity in some places, so the precise rate and pricing unit must be agreed before payment; stating one fixed price here would be misleading.

The day on the Argentine side is combined with a flight to Buenos Aires. Allow extra airport time after the border crossing and park visit. Water levels and weather can also affect access to individual walkways.

## Tango in Argentina and Chile's wineries

The [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) tour includes La Boca, San Telmo, Plaza de Mayo, the Obelisk, Recoleta and Puerto Madero. The evening tango show with dinner and wine is part of the program, but no separate guide is provided at the show. Trips to Tigre, a gaucho ranch and Montevideo remain optional and must fit into the short stop in the capital.

In Santiago, sightseeing covers the historic center, La Moneda Palace, Plaza de Armas, Santa Lucía Hill and modern districts. Travelers interested in wine may add a trip to the [Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/) with tasting for $230 per person, with a minimum of 2 participants. **This is an option, not a standard part of the tour.**

## Price, flights and accommodation conditions

The package includes nine nights with breakfasts, main excursions with Russian-speaking guides, transfers, a Champions' Parade ticket, the tango show with dinner, and flights **Rio–Iguazu–Buenos Aires–Santiago**. International flights to the start of the trip and homeward are paid separately. Optional excursions and Marius restaurant are also excluded.

We offer hotel categories of 3*, 4* and 5*, each with separate SGL, DBL and TPL rates. The lowest price starts **from $5208 per person** in a triple room at a 3* hotel. The Carnival-event ticket is already included in this package, an important distinction when comparing it with booking an independent trip to Rio for the same dates.

When choosing, look beyond the room category to how convenient it will be to return from the Sambadrome at night, the time of the following day's excursion and the baggage allowance on included flights. Services at specific hotels and parade seating are confirmed for the chosen package.

## Frequently asked questions about the Champions' Parade

### Is the Champions' Parade ticket included in the tour price?

Yes. Both the ticket and transfers from the hotel to the Sambadrome and back are included. The exact seating sector, pickup time and confirmed schedule are specified at booking.

### Are the Champions' Parade and the samba schools' competition parade the same event?

No. The Special Group's competition parades in 2027 are scheduled for February 7, 8 and 9, while the Champions' Parade is on February 13. This tour is dedicated specifically to the champions' evening.

### Are all flights already paid for?

Domestic and regional flights between Rio, Iguazu, Buenos Aires and Santiago are included. International flights to the start of the journey and the flight home are paid separately.

### Can Montevideo be added?

Yes. A trip across the Río de la Plata is available among the optional excursions from Buenos Aires. It costs extra, and its timing must be coordinated with the compulsory excursions and the flight to Chile.
